newsItems.title: Djokovic Breaks Federer's Wimbledon Match-Wins Record
newsItems.excerpt: Novak Djokovic wrote another chapter of Wimbledon history on Sunday, July 5, defeating qualifier Roman Safiullin 7-6 (8-6), 6-3, 3-6, 6-3 on Centre Court to claim his 106th men's singles match win at the All England Club and move one clear of Roger Federer's long-standing record. The 39-year-old seven-time champion, who matched Federer's mark in the third round, screamed through visible frustration at times — later calling the outbursts "meltdowns" — but served out the fourth set at love after Safiullin had pushed him hard in a spirited run that included an upset of 12th seed Andrey Rublev. The victory sent Djokovic into his 17th Wimbledon quarter-final, one behind Federer's men's record, and set up a last-eight clash with third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime, who survived a five-set thriller against Alejandro Davidovich Fokina featuring one of the best points of the tournament. Djokovic remains on course for a record 25th Grand Slam title and a potential semi-final meeting with defending champion Jannik Sinner, who advanced with a 6-3, 7-6 (7-0), 6-3 win over Japanese qualifier Shintaro Mochizuki.

newsItems.title: Syafiq Kamal Ends Seven-Year Wait with Mumbai PSA Title
newsItems.excerpt: Malaysia's Mohammad Syafiq Kamal finally returned to the winner's circle at a PSA event on Friday, July 3, rallying from two games down to defeat Egypt's second-seeded Yassin Shohdy 6-11, 9-11, 11-8, 14-12, 11-8 in the HCL-SRFI PSA Challenger final at Juhu Vile Parle Gymkhana in Mumbai. The world No. 156 had not lifted a PSA trophy since the SRAM PSA 1 event in Bukit Jalil in 2019 and gained sweet revenge over Shohdy, who beat him in the 2024 ACE Challenger 6K final in Kerteh. The Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia confirmed Syafiq's place in the national squad for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games from September 19 to October 4, though the 27-year-old insisted he cannot afford complacency with months of preparation still ahead. On the same card, India's Tanvi Khanna staged an equally dramatic comeback in the women's final, saving match point in the third game before beating Farida Walid 8-11, 2-11, 12-10, 11-9, 11-7 for her fifth PSA title in 11 final appearances. The Mumbai Challenger drew elite regional talent as the PSA calendar shifts toward the 2026-27 season opening in August.

newsItems.title: Hong Kit Wong Claims Third PPA Asia Singles Crown in Tokyo
newsItems.excerpt: Hong Kit Wong added another chapter to his breakout PPA Tour Asia season on Saturday, July 4, dismantling Mitchell Hargreaves 11-4, 11-3 in the Sansan Tokyo Open men's singles final at Arena Tachikawa Tachihi. The victory gave Wong his third professional singles title of the year after triumphs at the Hong Kong Open and Beijing Open, capping a $50,000 PPA Asia 500 event that drew more than 800 players across five pro disciplines in the Japanese capital. Hargreaves had reached the championship match with comeback wins over Tama Shimabukuro and Nasa Hatakeyama, but Wong's precision and pace proved too much in a straight-games decider. Rika Fujiwara earlier rallied past Pei Chuan Kao 7-11, 11-7, 12-10 for women's singles gold, Sahra Dennehy and Danni Elle Townsend took the women's doubles title, and Yuta Funemizu paired with Tama Shimabukuro for men's doubles glory. Attention now shifts to the inaugural PPA Asia 500 Singapore Open, scheduled for July 23–26 at The Sports Arina @ Expo with a $70,000 prize pool and 500 ranking points on offer.

newsItems.title: China Sweeps WTT US Smash Doubles as Singles Finals Loom
newsItems.excerpt: China dominated the doubles podiums at the WTT United States Smash 2026 on Saturday, July 4, at the Ontario Convention Center in Southern California, while the $1.55 million Grand Smash built toward singles finals featuring many of the sport's biggest names. Top-seeded Wang Manyu and Kuai Man edged Japan's Miwa Harimoto and Hina Hayata — fresh off winning the WTT Singapore Smash — 13-11, 4-11, 14-12, 11-8 in a tense women's doubles final, and Wen Ruibo and Yuan Licen recovered from a 2-1 deficit to beat top seeds Lin Shidong and Huang Youzheng 11-9, 8-11, 6-11, 11-7, 11-9 in an all-Chinese men's doubles decider. South Korea's Lim Jong-hoon and Shin Yu-bin had already claimed their first WTT Grand Smash mixed doubles crown by defeating Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha in five games. In singles, world No. 1 Sun Yingsha swept past Chen Xingtong 11-5, 11-5, 11-6, 11-6 to set up an all-Chinese women's semi-final against Wang Yidi, Kuai Man saved two match points in a seven-game epic against Hitomi Sato, and Truls Möregårdh, Felix Lebrun, Sora Matsushima, and Vladimir Sidorenko advanced in a wide-open men's draw after Wang Chuqin and Lin Shidong fell in the Round of 16.
